docs.title: Agents check each other before a deal
docs.body:
On Arc Testnet, a Karwan agent pays 0.01 USD over x402 to read the other
side's deal record before it commits. Payment settles through Circle Gateway.
The first live read ran on 16 October 2026.

A buyer's agent reads each seller's record before building the shortlist, and
a seller's agent reads the buyer's record before it bids. The seller's agent
passes on a buyer who has lost more disputes than they have completed, and
flags a new buyer on a large request for the seller to look at. The seller desk
shows what was paid and what the agent learned.

A record is read only when its owner has turned on Let agents check my record.
The details of a read are deleted after 24 hours, and the owner sees who read
their record. Others see a score, a tier and counts, never deal amounts or who
someone traded with.

Mainnet escrow is not enabled, so these checks run on testnet only.

docs.title: Assistant mode and Help
docs.body:
With Use assistant switched on, the whole account runs from one
conversation. You say what you want, your agent prepares it as a card, and
nothing moves until you confirm the card. Conversations are kept on your
account. A card from an earlier conversation shows whether it was done and
can never be confirmed again.

A deal is built the same way. Name the person and say what the deal is
for; the agent asks only for what is missing, such as the amount and when it
is due, says the usual terms in one line, and shows one card with every term,
goods terms included. Sending it moves no money. Once the other person
accepts, the payment card appears in the same conversation and in your
alerts, and the money moves only when you confirm it.

Deal insurance works the same way. Ask to take it out and the card shows the
amount, the 7-day wait and the day you can collect it; while it waits it no
longer protects your deals. You can ask to cancel the wait, and to collect it
once the wait ends.

Every step of a deal after it starts works the same way. You can change a
deal or counter it before money is in, take back a deal the seller has not
accepted, say the goods arrived, add review time, check a delivery yourself
when the delivery check has not answered, claim a payment the buyer left in
silence, ask a buyer to release, or answer that ask. On requests you can
make your own offer, withdraw it, take a seller's offer, and go ahead or pass
on a near match. You can edit your offer on the market, stop your agent
bidding on a request, and write in a deal's chat. In Telegram, the steps
that pay out or pay in open the Karwan page, where you confirm them.

Money works the same way. You can pay someone's payment link from your
balance, get free test USDC on testnet, have a transfer between networks
that has not arrived checked again or carried on, retry or cancel a money
move, have a deal payment that did not confirm checked again, pause money
leaving your account, and remove a saved payout address. With your own
wallet, you can also put money into deal insurance from the assistant; your
wallet asks you to sign. Resuming money out and adding a payout address stay
on the page, because they need your World ID.

Karwan is adding the remaining account actions to the assistant the same
way, so anything you can do on a page you can ask for.
The few steps that need your own device, such as a passkey, your Karwan PIN
or a World ID check, open their page instead.

A picture or PDF can be picked, pasted or dragged into the message box. It
waits there until you send, and shows in your message with the words you
typed beside it.

Help answers how things work and what went wrong, from what your account
shows. A person from the Karwan team joins the same conversation when you
ask for one, or when the assistant cannot do it, with the conversation so
far, so you do not repeat yourself.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: Colour
docs.body:
These are the published values, from the product's brand palette.

```
accent              #AFC95B    Karwan green: the one primary action, positive money state
ink / dark          #16202A    ink and dark surface
canvas              #EEF2F7    light theme canvas
paper               #FFFFFF    light cards and email
dark inset          #27313A
text sub on light   #646C74
text sub on dark    #A0A6AD
green text on light #42560F    lime-family text that stays readable on light
hairline on dark    rgba(206, 220, 232, 0.18)
```

The accent is a muted lime, softened so green fills do not glare and dark text
stays legible on top. Use it for one thing per screen. Status colours are
separate and always paired with words.

docs.title: Logo usage
docs.body:
Two assets: a wordmark and a mark, each in a light and a dark variant, shipped as
both SVG and PNG. Prefer the SVG anywhere it will render.

Pick the variant by the surface behind it, not by taste. The dark wordmark goes
on light surfaces, the light wordmark on dark. Never place either on the accent.

Do not recolour, rotate, outline, add a gradient, or set it against a busy
photograph. Give it clear space on all sides equal to the height of the mark.

Community use is welcome under these rules. What is not welcome is any use that
implies Karwan endorses a product, or any placement that could read as Karwan
having issued a statement it did not.

docs.title: Brand principles
docs.body:
Six rules, in order of how often they get broken.

**Calm and legible.** Karwan is where strangers put money in escrow with each
other, so the interface earns trust: calm like a good financial product, never
a generated template. One job and one primary action per screen.

**Money is the loudest thing.** The amount is the largest line, in tabular
figures with the currency written out: `1,200.00 USDC`, never `$1,200`. Next
loudest is the next action and whose move it is.

**One accent, used once.** Lime is for the one primary action and positive
money state. A page with three lime elements has no primary action.

**Sentence case, plain words.** No shouting labels. Brackets and mono are only
for technical metadata such as references and proof rows. Request and offer,
never brief or bid. No em dashes.

**Hairlines, not stacked cards.** Facts sit in label and value rows separated by
thin lines. Forms stay in a narrow reading column.

**Honest states and no internals.** Sending is never shown as failed. Chain ids,
addresses and protocol names stay behind "Proof on Arc". Motion only explains
change and respects reduced motion. On desktop a mouse wheel glides the page to
a stop; phones keep their own scrolling.

**Line drawings, not stock.** Pictures are pencil or line drawings of real
trade: two people dealing, goods, the money held between them, the record that
follows. No stock photos, generated imagery, gradients or mixed styles.

docs.title: Typography
docs.body:
One family: General Sans. Hierarchy comes from size and weight, not from a
second face or from capitals.

**Headings.** Sentence case, weight 500 to 600, slightly tight tracking.

**Money.** Tabular figures, the amount larger than anything around it, the
currency written after it.

**Metadata.** The same family with tabular figures. Uppercase letterspaced
labels and brackets are reserved for technical metadata such as references,
network names and timestamps, never for section titles or prose.

Email uses the system sans stack with the same rules.

docs.title: Confirming it is you, with a passkey or a Karwan PIN
docs.body:
A person's agents run their deals for them: they pay into a deal, accept,
deliver and release inside the limits the person set, so a deal keeps moving
while the person is away. Karwan asks the person to be present for three
things only, and then they confirm with a passkey, which is their phone's
face or fingerprint check, or with a 6-digit Karwan PIN.

The three things: setting up their Karwan record and their buying agent's
limits, putting up deal insurance, and money leaving Karwan for an address
that is not one of their own Karwan wallets. Putting up deal insurance is
the consent for it to protect their buyers and back advances from
financiers on their deals, so taking an advance later is one tap.

Five wrong PINs lock the PIN for 15 minutes, and a passkey still works in
the meantime. A forgotten PIN is reset with a code sent to the person's
email. A PIN is never typed into a chat: the agent sends a one-time Karwan
link and the person confirms on that page. Someone who signs in with their
own wallet confirms by signing in that wallet.

Each confirmation fits one action and one amount, and works once.

docs.title: The credit passport
docs.body:
A public page per business, built from settled deals, repayment behaviour and
counterparty concentration. It follows the wallet, not the platform.

Standing has to be earned in completed work. Stake, tenure and activity all raise
the score on their own, which is deliberate, but they cannot carry a tier without
settled deals behind it. Concentration caps the tier when most of those deals are
with a single counterparty, so trading in a circle cannot manufacture a record.

Both matter because the tier is not cosmetic. It decides financing eligibility
and how much collateral a supplier posts against an advance, and a ladder that is
cheap to climb makes the financing gate cheap to fake.

It is also a paid endpoint. Any lender can pay a fraction of a cent over x402 and
read a verifiable settled-deal record without asking Karwan for permission.

docs.title: What counts as delivery
docs.body:
Delivery has to be against something the buyer can check.

A service delivers a link, and the host has to resolve in DNS before the delivery
is accepted. Carrying an https scheme proved nothing on its own: an invented
domain satisfied every earlier check.

Physical goods deliver a carrier and a tracking reference that opens a page the
buyer can read. The buyer then confirms arrival as a separate act from releasing
the money, because arrival is a fact about the shipment and release is a decision
about the money.

Karwan does not verify the shipment with the carrier. What it requires is that
the claim is specific and on the record rather than absent.

docs.title: Deposit and withdraw
docs.body:
Money moves in and out of Arc on one screen. What that screen asks for depends on
who holds the funds, and the difference is the point rather than an inconsistency.

An account that signs in with email or a passkey gets one address. Copy it, send
USDC from Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Avalanche or Unichain,
and the balance updates itself.
There is no chain to choose, no amount to declare and no wallet to connect,
because Circle derives every deposit wallet from that user's identity anchor, so
the same address serves all seven. Solana has its own address on the same screen: a
different signature curve cannot share one.

An account that connects its own wallet keeps the explicit flow. It holds the
funds, so it picks the chain the USDC is on and signs the transfer.

Withdrawals reach Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon and Solana, and
never require that chain's gas token to receive.

The word for this is Deposit and Withdraw. Not top up, not add money, not cash
out, and never the name of the transfer protocol underneath: which rail carries a
move is not something a person sending money needs to hold in their head.

docs.title: Escrow families for every kind of trade
docs.body:
Karwan's next escrow contracts are deployed on Arc Testnet and not on mainnet.
A timelock owns them, so every rule change waits a day in public, queued by a
multi-signature owner. The Karwan app does not use them yet.

Arc limits each contract to 24,576 bytes, so escrow is split into families,
each holding only its own deals' money, so a fault in one cannot reach another
family's balance. Agreement covers fixed-price goods and services with up to 12
tranches, instalment plans and disputes that freeze only the disputed part.
Time covers hourly, daily and retainer work, cycle by cycle. Jobs covers
ERC-8183 jobs, bounties and contests.

Shared pieces sit behind them: a hub that holds no money, an identity registry
with 7-day recovery, one dispute clock, a stake vault and a timelock. Chainlink
CRE workflows for delivery checks and timeouts run end to end in the CRE
simulator on an Arc fork and are not deployed.

They go live on mainnet only after an external audit.

docs.title: What stops the other side taking my money
docs.body:
The money sits in an escrow contract, not with Karwan and not with your
counterparty. A buyer funds it before work starts, so a supplier can see the
money exists before shipping. A supplier cannot take it early, and a buyer cannot
withdraw it once the deal is accepted.

The final tranche always needs an explicit buyer click. Nothing settles the last
portion on a timer.

If the two sides disagree, either can raise a dispute, which freezes the escrow.
A dispute is resolved by an arbiter that splits the unreleased funds by
proportion rather than picking a winner, and that arbiter is a 2-of-3 Safe, so no
single person can move a disputed deal.

docs.title: Core terms
docs.body:
**Escrow.** A contract that holds the buyer's money while the work happens. It
releases against delivery, in milestones, and nobody can pull funds out of turn.

**Milestone.** One slice of a deal. A deal splits into two to five. The last one
always needs the buyer to click.

**Credit passport.** A public page built from a business's settled deals and
repayment behaviour. It belongs to the wallet, so it moves with the business
rather than living on the platform.

**Factoring.** Selling an invoice for less than face to be paid now instead of on
settlement. The discount is the cost of the wait.

**Purchase-order financing.** Working capital advanced before delivery, against a
purchase order whose escrow is already funded.

**Receivable assignment.** Recording, on the escrow, that a financier is paid
ahead of the supplier at settlement. It is what makes financing non-recourse: the
financier is repaid by the contract rather than by chasing the supplier.

**x402.** A payment standard for machine-to-machine calls, used here so an agent
can pay a fraction of a cent for a single piece of data.

**USYC.** A tokenised T-bill fund. Idle balance is parked in it so capital earns
while it waits.

docs.title: How Karwan is built
docs.body:
Karwan is building one reputation for the internet, starting with its open
market. In the open market, freelancers, people trading goods and services, and
small businesses make agreements locally and across borders. Every agreement is
protected by escrow and leaves a record that travels with the person, and trade
finance (purchase-order financing and invoice factoring) sits on the same
escrow. It starts in Nigeria, then the regions behind Karwan's five languages:
Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. It is meant to feel like a normal
banking app.

The work is organised in six tracks, built one roadmap item at a time: finding
and agreeing a deal, protected deals, reputation that travels, trade finance,
money that works like a bank account, and the channels where people talk to
their agent. Each track is described in Karwan's public architecture views,
with what is live, built and planned.

Some things wait until the core market works end to end: partner and developer
pages wait for unified reputation, and the newsletter waits for a full working
product. Do not describe parked work as available.

docs.title: Invoice factoring
docs.body:
The supplier asks to be paid early, naming a floor if they want one. Financiers
then bid a discount against the supplier's reputation tier, and the supplier
accepts one or ignores them all.

Nothing reaches a financier until that request exists. An invoice is never listed
for funding on the strength of the supplier having opened a deal, because that
would publish their counterparty, amount and timing to every approved financier
without anybody asking to be funded.

Offers are priced against what the escrow can still pay, not the invoice face.
Face includes the platform fee and every tranche already released, and the
financier is only ever repaid out of what is left. On settlement the escrow pays
the financier ahead of the supplier, so repayment is not something anyone chases.

All of it can also be done by asking the Karwan assistant, on the website or in
Telegram: the supplier asks to be paid early, reads the offers ranked as the deal
page ranks them, and takes or turns one down; a financier sees the requests they
may fund and makes an offer, which is refused before anything moves if their
wallet does not hold the advance. Taking an offer and making one are confirmed on
Karwan, where every figure is shown before money moves.

Being paid early is not yet open on deals made on Karwan's new escrow. Deals made
before it can use it now.

docs.title: Local payout corridors
docs.body:
Local bank payout corridors are planned and are not live in the current Arc
Testnet release. A local trade can be created today, but its present settlement
uses test USDC.

Karwan plans to keep USDC as the cross-border settlement layer while approved
payout infrastructure converts to local currency. Each corridor must pass
availability, compliance, recipient, fee, foreign-exchange, reconciliation,
refund and support gates before launch.

docs.title: Message anyone by their Karwan tag
docs.body:
A person can ask their agent to message someone by Karwan tag before any
deal, for example "send @ada a message: do you make agbada?". Ada gets it in
her Karwan chat, with an alert on Telegram and by email, and sees the sender's
tag, country and tier. She answers with her agent's help.

When they agree, either agent starts the protected deal. Money never moves
from a message. A message with a phone number, an email or a link, sent
before any deal between the two, carries a warning to keep payment in Karwan
escrow. Someone whose first messages to five people in a day all go
unanswered is paused from writing to anyone new for a day, and three messages
in a row with no answer wait for a reply. Only someone with a Karwan tag can
message, and a message with a link Karwan flags is not sent. Messages are kept
14 days.

This is built for testnet and not live.

docs.title: Milestone escrow
docs.body:
A deal splits into two to five milestones. The supplier marks a milestone
delivered, the buyer reviews and releases that portion.

The final milestone always needs an explicit buyer click and never releases on a
timer. That is the buyer protection the rest of the product rests on, and it is
enforced in the contract rather than in the interface.

A missed deadline lets the buyer reclaim, and the miss lands on the supplier's
record. A cancel or extension both sides agree to carries no penalty and refunds
in full. The platform fee is 1.5 percent of the deal, split evenly between the
two sides.

docs.title: Your agent negotiates while you sleep
docs.body:
Post what you need in the assistant, on the website or Telegram, and you can
close the chat. Your agent asks sellers for offers and negotiates, and the
assistant writes back in the same conversation, and on Telegram, only when
something moves: offers in, your shortlist ready with the seller the agent
recommends, a near match when nothing fits your budget, an agreed deal, the
money locked, the work delivered.

When you post, you can turn on Agree for me. Your agent then agrees with the
seller it recommends, within your budget, and you wake up to an agreed deal
ready for one tap to lock the money. It never agrees above your budget and
never moves money on its own.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: Open trade-finance market
docs.body:
A broader quote market for eligible Karwan-originated receivables and purchase
orders is planned. Invoice factoring, purchase-order financing and the financier
desk exist in the current testnet build, while the broader open market does not.

The supplier will compare the advance, repayment, spread, expiry, recourse and
concentration controls, then choose whether to accept. Karwan does not finance
arbitrary outside invoices and does not guarantee an advance.

docs.title: Sharing your full passport
docs.body:
Your passport is sealed: other people see your standing and a few plain
reasons, never your numbers. When someone asks to see your record before a
deal, you can show them the full passport you see yourself, amounts and the
money held as a reserve included.

Open your passport and tap Share full record, or ask your assistant on the
website, Telegram or WhatsApp. Choose one person by their Karwan tag, who must
be signed in to open it, or a link anyone can open, for someone not on Karwan
yet. Choose 24 hours or 7 days.

Your passport lists each live share, who it is for, until when and how often it
was opened. Stop any of them at any time; the link then shows the sealed
passport again. At most five shares are live at once.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: Photos on offers
docs.body:
An offer on Karwan's market can carry up to four photos, so a buyer sees the
item before agreeing a deal. The first photo shows on the market card and all
of them on the offer page.

You add photos on the offer form, or send them to your assistant before it
drafts the offer. You say so in the words you send with it, for example
"selling this" or "for my offer", on the website or in Telegram. On the
website a photo sent with no words asks whether it is for an offer. The assistant's offer card shows how many photos it adds, and nothing
is posted until you confirm.

Photos are resized on your device before they are sent, which also drops the
location data a phone camera adds. Anyone signed in can report an offer or
its photos from the offer page, and the team reviews every report.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: Purchase-order financing
docs.body:
Working capital advanced against an accepted purchase order whose escrow the
buyer has already funded.

The advance goes straight to the supplier, in the same transaction that redirects
that deal's settlement to the financier. That atomicity is the whole design.
There is no state in which the redirect is live and the supplier has not been
paid, so nothing can strand the advance, and the supplier can spend the capital
immediately. An advance they cannot touch until after they deliver is not working
capital.

On settlement the escrow pays the financier ahead of the supplier. If the deal
settles short, the shortfall alone is recovered from the supplier's staked
collateral, and the rest of the bond returns to them.

docs.title: Network and contracts
docs.body:
Karwan runs on Arc Testnet, chain 5042002, where USDC is the gas token.

Every contract in the live bundle is verified on the explorer. The escrow's
arbiter is a 2-of-3 Safe, so a disputed escrow cannot be resolved by one key.

Contract addresses are published and readable by anyone. Treat the explorer as
the source of truth on any disagreement with a document: the chain is the record,
and a page describing it is a copy.

On Arc mainnet, chain 5042, two Karwan contracts are live and verified on
Sourcify, both owned by a 2-of-3 Safe: KarwanReputation at
0xa8E41F941b44CA091E3Ab7b600fe1484838aE27D, which records completed deal
outcomes, and KarwanBusinessRegistry at
0x69eA60B6EFd13A126Eb00d25aB0f21A4AfC636eF, which records that a business's
documents were checked, storing only a document hash. Neither holds customer
money. Mainnet escrow is not enabled until the contracts and backend pass an
external audit.

docs.title: Ratings after a settled deal
docs.body:
After a deal settles on Karwan, each person's agent asks them to rate the
other from 1 to 5, with an optional note, and reminds them once after three
days. A rating shows as soon as it is given.

Each person's public rating is the average of the ratings shown, with how
many there are, for example "4.8 from 23 deals". Under three ratings it shows
"New". Only the two people in a settled deal can rate it, once each, within 14 days
of it settling. Ratings from disputed deals are counted beside the number,
for example "3.7 from 3 deals, 2 disputed". A note with a phone number, an email
or a link is kept private.

The rating is separate from the reputation score and does not change it.
Agents use it when ranking people, after skill fit, location and
verification.

This is built for testnet and not live.

docs.title: Review windows and release timing
docs.body:
The review window is not one fixed number.

It grows with the size of the deal and shrinks as two parties build a settled
history together. On a goods deal it cannot expire while the shipment is still in
transit, and agreed Net terms hold it open for the full term. Marking goods
delivered means dispatched, not arrived.

The same window governs the unattended release and the seller's own claim. When
those two disagreed, the protection was one button wide: a Net 30 deal held off
the automatic release for thirty days while the seller could force the payout on
day one.

Nothing in the window keys off quality. The contract cannot observe whether the
work was any good, and a timer that pretended to would be a slower way of
guessing.

docs.title: Setting up Karwan the way you use it
docs.body:
After agent wallets are active, Karwan asks what you want it to do: get paid
for your work, sell products, buy or hire, run business deals, or build a
record clients trust. It then asks only what those answers need, such as
what you do, your usual price and how fast you deliver, how your clients
usually pay you, and where you are.
It shows the result as "Here's your Karwan" and saves nothing until you
say it looks right. The same questions run on the website, in Telegram, and
from a conversation with your agent.

Three answers change what your agents do. If you only work with clients you
already have, your selling agent stays off the market. If you choose "Ask me
first", it does not make offers on its own: it tells you about a request that
fits and you decide. "How should we reach you" picks Telegram, email or both.
Money never moves without your confirmation.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: Reputation lookups from connected social accounts
docs.body:
Karwan plans to let a person connect their social accounts, so an agent can
find their Karwan record by handle. A buyer could ask their agent to check a
Telegram username and get back that person's tier, reasons and counts.

Connecting an account will be optional, in the agent workspace, and only with
the person's consent. Ownership is proven by signing in where the network
offers it, or by placing a code on the profile where it does not, so a link
alone never claims someone else's account. A linked handle is not proof of
identity.

This is not built yet. No network is a partner, and none is named as one.

docs.title: Trade Anywhere browser companion
docs.body:
A user-invoked browser companion for starting a protected trade beside a
supported website is planned and is not live in the current Arc Testnet release.

Trade Anywhere will create a user-approved trade draft and secure invite, with X
as the first focused surface. The counterparty will be able to review, counter or
accept through normal Karwan web without installing the companion.

It will not scrape private messages, inject social actions, post, follow, like,
reply or send messages for the user.

docs.title: Unified reputation
docs.body:
Karwan is building one reputation that travels with a person across platforms.
This is the direction the rest of the product serves, and it is not live in the
current Arc Testnet release.

People join a new marketplace, job board or region and vet themselves from zero
every time, because their record is split across platforms that do not talk to
each other. Unified reputation brings that record together: easy to track, easy
to look up, hard to fake. It starts with Karwan's market, whose completed
deals are the first and most heavily weighted input.

Agents will work only with data a person already owns, after they connect a
source and agree. Nothing is leaked, sold or scraped, and consent can be
withdrawn. Other platforms join as partners once the working model is designed
with them; none is named until an agreement exists. The reputation layer is
being built on Circle's agent stack, while escrow, staking and Circle's payment
tools bring the market on chain.

Today a person's Karwan reputation comes only from completed Karwan deals.

docs.title: The ways you deal
docs.body:
Your agents work from the ways you deal, for selling and for buying. Each way
is one kind of deal with its own price and time: one-time, milestones paid in
stages, goods with delivery, where review starts when the item arrives, and a
refundable deposit, like a rental. A goods way also says where you ship and
how long it takes to arrive. Other kinds of escrow are added as they go live.

Your selling agent offers on a request inside the way of its kind. When a
buyer asks for a kind of deal you have not listed, the agent does not offer
on its own: it tells you about the request and you decide.

Setup starts you with one way, from how your clients usually pay you. You
add, change or remove ways on your profile or by telling your agent, and
nothing is saved until you confirm. Money never moves without your
confirmation.

This is built for testnet and not live yet.

docs.title: What Karwan is
docs.body:
Karwan unifies online reputation, starting with an open market for secure local
and cross-border trade. People join a new marketplace, job board or region and
have to vet themselves from zero every time; Karwan is building one reputation
that travels with a person, so hidden talent becomes visible and opportunity
follows. It starts with Karwan's market, where every completed deal is
protected in escrow and recorded.

People and businesses can buy or sell services, goods, supplies and eligible
business orders. A trade may be local, with both parties in the same country,
or cross-border, with parties in different countries.

Trade can start as a direct deal with a known counterparty, an email invite, an
open buyer request, an open seller offer, a verified business connection or an
agent-assisted match. The parties agree the commercial terms before test USDC
moves into milestone escrow on Arc Testnet. Money sits in the escrow contract,
not with Karwan or the counterparty, and releases against the agreed outcome.

Individual and business trade use the same protection layer. Business accounts
can also build a portable credit record from settled trade and request financing
for eligible Karwan-originated accepted invoices or purchase orders. Financing
is opt-in: approved financiers quote terms and the supplier chooses. Direct deals
remain available without verification, while agent matching, verified-business
features and financing may have eligibility gates.

The current release is testnet software. Local trade does not mean local-currency
payment is live. Unified reputation across platforms, browser capture, mainnet
settlement and local bank payout are planned expansion, not current capabilities.

docs.title: When a buyer does not respond after delivery
docs.body:
On deals held by Karwan's escrow family, no payment goes to a seller only
because the buyer's review time ran out, since a buyer may simply be away.

When review time ends without the buyer releasing the payment or raising a
problem, the seller is asked whether to ask for payment, in one tap on the
deal page or from their assistant in any chat. If they have not asked
within 24 hours, their selling agent asks for them and tells them.

The buyer then has 72 hours to answer by saying what is wrong with the
delivery. An answer sends the case to a person on Karwan's review team,
who rules within 5 days; if they do not, the deal's agreed fallback share
applies. With no answer, that payment goes to the seller. This works the
same for a milestone and for the final payment.

A buyer opens a dispute while their review time runs; after it ends they
answer the seller's instead.

On Arc Testnet this is how Karwan runs these deals once new deals are
switched over to the escrow family. The contract itself will carry the
rule in the mainnet release, before its external audit.

docs.title: World ID only when the risk calls for it
docs.body:
On an agent deal on Arc Testnet, Karwan's trust rules ask a person to confirm
with World ID only for one of four reasons: their first deal, a deal of 1,000
USDC or more, many deals from a new account in one day, or a link they sent
earlier that was judged malicious.

The buyer confirms when choosing an offer. The seller confirms before escrow
funds, and escrow funds as soon as they pass. A person who already passed World
ID anywhere on Karwan is not asked again for a first deal.

A price far from the market, a low score or a link judged only suspicious never
asks for World ID. Replayed over 197 testnet deals, these rules asked on 55
deals, down from 97 under the earlier rules.

On testnet the check can be skipped so testing is never blocked. World ID is
not configured on mainnet, where escrow is not enabled yet.

docs.title: Your Karwan record, set up once
docs.body:
Deals held by Karwan's escrow family count on each side's Karwan record. A
person sets their record up once: before their first payment as a buyer,
and as a seller when they agree to their first deal's terms or before their
selling agent offers on a request. Setting it up links their buying and
selling agents to it. The buying agent can then pay up to 1,005 USDC at a
time and 10,000 USDC in total for one year, and asks to be renewed after
that.

A seller sets it up when they agree because the escrow notes each side's
record at the moment the buyer pays in. A deal paid in before the seller
had a record runs normally but does not count on the seller's record.
Until a seller has a record, their selling agent does not offer on new
requests and tells them once a day.

It takes one confirmation with a passkey or a Karwan PIN, or, for someone
who signs in with their own wallet, signing in that wallet. In Telegram the
card shows in the chat and the confirmation happens on Karwan.

After each payment on a deal, the seller's earnings move from their selling
agent to their own wallet; a move that is still waiting shows in their
balance and is tried again. Once a deal settles, the deal page says when it
is on both records. Deals can be up to 1,000 USDC while Karwan is in beta.

This runs on Arc Testnet once new deals are switched over to the escrow
family; mainnet follows an external audit.

facts.title: Agents check each other before a deal
facts.summary: On Arc Testnet, a Karwan agent pays 0.01 USD over x402 to read the other side's deal record before it commits. Payment settles through Circle Gateway. The first live read ran on 16 October 2026.

check.note: The seller's agent reads the buyer's record and passes when disputes lost outnumber completed deals.

facts.title: Assistant mode and Help
facts.summary: With Use assistant switched on, the whole account runs from one conversation. You say what you want, your agent prepares it as a card, and nothing moves until you confirm the card. Conversations are kept on your account. A card from an earlier conversation shows whether it was done and can never be confirmed again.

facts.title: Colour
facts.summary: These are the published values, from the product's brand palette.

facts.title: Logo usage
facts.summary: Two assets: a wordmark and a mark, each in a light and a dark variant, shipped as both SVG and PNG. Prefer the SVG anywhere it will render.

facts.title: Brand principles
facts.summary: Six rules, in order of how often they get broken.

facts.title: Typography
facts.summary: One family: General Sans. Hierarchy comes from size and weight, not from a second face or from capitals.

facts.title: Confirming it is you, with a passkey or a Karwan PIN
facts.summary: A person's agents run their deals for them: they pay into a deal, accept, deliver and release inside the limits the person set, so a deal keeps moving while the person is away. Karwan asks the person to be present for three things only, and then they confirm with a passkey, which is their phone's face or fingerprint check, or with a 6-digit Karwan PIN.

facts.title: The credit passport
facts.summary: A public page per business, built from settled deals, repayment behaviour and counterparty concentration. It follows the wallet, not the platform.

check.note: Concentration caps the tier, so a record built on one counterparty cannot buy standing.

facts.title: What counts as delivery
facts.summary: Delivery has to be against something the buyer can check.

check.note: Goods deliveries are refused without a carrier and tracking reference.

facts.title: Deposit and withdraw
facts.summary: Money moves in and out of Arc on one screen. What that screen asks for depends on who holds the funds, and the difference is the point rather than an inconsistency.

check.note: Returns at most two DISTINCT addresses and no Circle blockchain code, so the chain vocabulary cannot reach a user.

facts.title: Escrow families for every kind of trade
facts.summary: Karwan's next escrow contracts are deployed on Arc Testnet and not on mainnet. A timelock owns them, so every rule change waits a day in public, queued by a multi-signature owner. The Karwan app does not use them yet.

facts.title: What stops the other side taking my money
facts.summary: The money sits in an escrow contract, not with Karwan and not with your counterparty. A buyer funds it before work starts, so a supplier can see the money exists before shipping. A supplier cannot take it early, and a buyer cannot withdraw it once the deal is accepted.

facts.title: Core terms
facts.summary: **Escrow.** A contract that holds the buyer's money while the work happens. It releases against delivery, in milestones, and nobody can pull funds out of turn.

facts.title: How Karwan is built
facts.summary: Karwan is building one reputation for the internet, starting with its open market. In the open market, freelancers, people trading goods and services, and small businesses make agreements locally and across borders. Every agreement is protected by escrow and leaves a record that travels with the person, and trade finance (purchase-order financing and invoice factoring) sits on the same escrow. It starts in Nigeria, then the regions behind Karwan's five languages: Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. It is meant to feel like a normal banking app.

check.note: How Karwan is built and its direction, from docs/architecture/00-direction.md; read against that file.

facts.title: Invoice factoring
facts.summary: The supplier asks to be paid early, naming a floor if they want one. Financiers then bid a discount against the supplier's reputation tier, and the supplier accepts one or ignores them all.

check.note: An invoice reaches no financier until the seller has asked.

facts.title: Local payout corridors
facts.summary: Local bank payout corridors are planned and are not live in the current Arc Testnet release. A local trade can be created today, but its present settlement uses test USDC.

facts.title: Message anyone by their Karwan tag
facts.summary: A person can ask their agent to message someone by Karwan tag before any deal, for example "send @ada a message: do you make agbada?". Ada gets it in her Karwan chat, with an alert on Telegram and by email, and sees the sender's tag, country and tier. She answers with her agent's help.

facts.title: Milestone escrow
facts.summary: A deal splits into two to five milestones. The supplier marks a milestone delivered, the buyer reviews and releases that portion.

check.note: The final release is a distinct buyer-called path, never reachable from a timer.

facts.title: Your agent negotiates while you sleep
facts.summary: Post what you need in the assistant, on the website or Telegram, and you can close the chat. Your agent asks sellers for offers and negotiates, and the assistant writes back in the same conversation, and on Telegram, only when something moves: offers in, your shortlist ready with the seller the agent recommends, a near match when nothing fits your budget, an agreed deal, the money locked, the work delivered.

facts.title: Open trade-finance market
facts.summary: A broader quote market for eligible Karwan-originated receivables and purchase orders is planned. Invoice factoring, purchase-order financing and the financier desk exist in the current testnet build, while the broader open market does not.

facts.title: Sharing your full passport
facts.summary: Your passport is sealed: other people see your standing and a few plain reasons, never your numbers. When someone asks to see your record before a deal, you can show them the full passport you see yourself, amounts and the money held as a reserve included.

facts.title: Photos on offers
facts.summary: An offer on Karwan's market can carry up to four photos, so a buyer sees the item before agreeing a deal. The first photo shows on the market card and all of them on the offer page.

facts.title: Purchase-order financing
facts.summary: Working capital advanced against an accepted purchase order whose escrow the buyer has already funded.

check.note: fund() pays the seller and assigns the receivable in one transaction.

facts.title: Network and contracts
facts.summary: Karwan runs on Arc Testnet, chain 5042002, where USDC is the gas token.

check.note: Reads the deployed escrow, so a stale address cannot pass.

facts.title: Ratings after a settled deal
facts.summary: After a deal settles on Karwan, each person's agent asks them to rate the other from 1 to 5, with an optional note, and reminds them once after three days. A rating shows as soon as it is given.

facts.title: Review windows and release timing
facts.summary: The review window is not one fixed number.

check.note: One window governs both the unattended release and the seller claim.

facts.title: Setting up Karwan the way you use it
facts.summary: After agent wallets are active, Karwan asks what you want it to do: get paid for your work, sell products, buy or hire, run business deals, or build a record clients trust. It then asks only what those answers need, such as what you do, your usual price and how fast you deliver, how your clients usually pay you, and where you are. It shows the result as "Here's your Karwan" and saves nothing until you say it looks right. The same questions run on the website, in Telegram, and from a conversation with your agent.

facts.title: Reputation lookups from connected social accounts
facts.summary: Karwan plans to let a person connect their social accounts, so an agent can find their Karwan record by handle. A buyer could ask their agent to check a Telegram username and get back that person's tier, reasons and counts.

facts.title: Trade Anywhere browser companion
facts.summary: A user-invoked browser companion for starting a protected trade beside a supported website is planned and is not live in the current Arc Testnet release.

facts.title: Unified reputation
facts.summary: Karwan is building one reputation that travels with a person across platforms. This is the direction the rest of the product serves, and it is not live in the current Arc Testnet release.

facts.title: The ways you deal
facts.summary: Your agents work from the ways you deal, for selling and for buying. Each way is one kind of deal with its own price and time: one-time, milestones paid in stages, goods with delivery, where review starts when the item arrives, and a refundable deposit, like a rental. A goods way also says where you ship and how long it takes to arrive. Other kinds of escrow are added as they go live.

facts.title: What Karwan is
facts.summary: Karwan unifies online reputation, starting with an open market for secure local and cross-border trade. People join a new marketplace, job board or region and have to vet themselves from zero every time; Karwan is building one reputation that travels with a person, so hidden talent becomes visible and opportunity follows. It starts with Karwan's market, where every completed deal is protected in escrow and recorded.

facts.title: When a buyer does not respond after delivery
facts.summary: On deals held by Karwan's escrow family, no payment goes to a seller only because the buyer's review time ran out, since a buyer may simply be away.

facts.title: World ID only when the risk calls for it
facts.summary: On an agent deal on Arc Testnet, Karwan's trust rules ask a person to confirm with World ID only for one of four reasons: their first deal, a deal of 1,000 USDC or more, many deals from a new account in one day, or a link they sent earlier that was judged malicious.

check.note: The four reasons that ask for World ID, and the pass that stops a busy new account being asked twice in a day.

facts.title: Your Karwan record, set up once
facts.summary: Deals held by Karwan's escrow family count on each side's Karwan record. A person sets their record up once: before their first payment as a buyer, and as a seller when they agree to their first deal's terms or before their selling agent offers on a request. Setting it up links their buying and selling agents to it. The buying agent can then pay up to 1,005 USDC at a time and 10,000 USDC in total for one year, and asks to be renewed after that.
